payload.why_this_raises_the_severity: The prior-day set is not trailing residue at the edge of the prune window — it is 32 of 36 files, the MAJORITY of the directory, spanning 02:20 through 21:05. Because the producer runs a fixed 15-min cadence every day, yesterday's filename set and today's are drawn from very nearly the same pool. So the directory is pre-seeded RIGHT NOW with a stale decoy at nearly every tick name today will use for the next ~19 hours. Under the current key-lookup, hitting 24h-old macro data is the default path and a clean miss is the exception. The only thing standing between that and a consumer acting on day-old macro data is each consumer's own inside-the-file date check — which is per-consumer, is not written down as a contract anywhere, and no future consumer is obliged to implement.
payload.fix_shape_unchanged: po_fold_20260825 already settled it: drop the key lookup, take the NEWEST cycle-snapshot-*.json inside the <=7min freshness gate both copies already specify. That is immune to the entire decoy population and does not depend on the prune at all. This amendment proposes NO new shape — it argues the settled shape is worth more than P1.
payload.prune_note: Still not a prune bug, and still do NOT widen the age threshold. The prune window (1440 min) equals the filename namespace period (1440 min) by construction, so every HH:MM name has a same-named prior-day twin alive in its final minutes. Pruning by DATE would remove the twins; widening the threshold makes it worse. If the freshness-gate fix lands, neither change is needed.
payload.still_do_not_do: Do NOT 'fix' this by rounding the producer's filename to the nominal tick. po_fold_20260825 already withdrew that shape — it would make the producer's name collide with the prior day's EXACTLY rather than approximately, which is the wrong direction.
